title: B200 flex_attention_fwd 18% performance regression after compiler change
body: We are seeing an approximately 18% regression in flex_attention_fwd compiled TFLOPs on an NVIDIA B200 after b3b9931cb7ed07a6d7a3833c8dcb7b7b519e882f. TritonBench averaged 440.059 compiled TFLOPs on ea4bdaf9d662e36a52ea422a37daa4e2e1abad30, immediately before that change, and 361.888 TFLOPs on b3b9931cb7ed07a6d7a3833c8dcb7b7b519e882f. Individual noop attention cases at sequence lengths 2048, 4096, and 8192 all regress. I also shared a standalone script containing the generated flex_attention_fwd kernel.

symptoms_visible: On my B200, flex_attention_fwd averages 440.059 compiled TFLOPs on the commit immediately before b3b9931 and 361.888 TFLOPs on b3b9931.
The noop cases with sequence lengths 2048, 4096, and 8192 all have higher compiled latency and lower compiled TFLOPs on the newer commit.
N0.label: N0 B200 performance regression reported

symptoms_visible: My comparison shows unchanged TTGIR, but the bad build has more shared-memory traffic and more load/store instructions.
In the generated PTX, the prominent 128x64xbf16 conversion uses ld.shared/st.shared in the good build and ldmatrix/stmatrix in the bad build.
N1.label: N1 compiler outputs and NCU traces compared

symptoms_visible: With a local hack that forces the conversion to lower through ld/st instead of ldmatrix/stmatrix, I measure 442 TFLOPs, versus 435 for the good baseline and 359 for the bad baseline.
N2.label: N2 alternate lowering benchmarked

symptoms_visible: Disabling the optimize_tmem_layouts pass gives me 435 TFLOPs instead of the approximately 359 TFLOPs from the regressed build.
N3.label: N3 responsible pass isolated

symptoms_visible: The installed regressed build still runs around 359 TFLOPs, and I narrowed the pass-level behavior to TMemLoadReducePattern.
N4.label: N4 pattern isolated and fix proposed

symptoms_visible: After testing the merged fix on my B200, the three compiled cases reach 458.404, 502.710, and 523.399 TFLOPs, averaging 494.838 TFLOPs.
N_terminal.label: terminal performance restored

question_patterns: Can you compare the TTGIR generated by the good and bad commits?
Does the compiler IR change across the regression boundary?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I compared the TTGIR from the commit before the regression and the commit with it. The TTGIR is unchanged.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The TTGIR changes substantially, including a new conversion in the attention loop that is already present before PTX lowering.

question_patterns: Can you diff the generated PTX and compare profiler traces from the good and bad commits?
Which generated instructions or hardware counters change significantly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The PTX differs mainly around a conversion: the good version lowers it to ld.shared/st.shared, while the bad version uses ldmatrix/stmatrix and has more load/store instructions. A 128x64xbf16 conversion in the loop stands out, and my NCU comparison shows a huge increase in shared-memory traffic.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The PTX is effectively identical and the NCU traces show no meaningful difference in shared-memory traffic or instruction counts.
The same conversion and shared-memory traffic increase appear, but the exact instruction counts vary slightly between runs.

question_patterns: Can you share the compiler outputs used for the comparison?
Please provide the TTGIR and the PTX from both builds.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I shared one TTGIR gist and separate PTX gists for the good and bad builds.

edges.comment: From c7-c10. Participant4 performed the TTGIR, PTX, and NCU comparison and shared the artifacts; that collaborator is folded into the simulated user side. The answers preserve the measured output rather than asserting the engineer's later root-cause interpretation.

question_patterns: Can you test an alternate lowering for the conversion and rerun the benchmark?
Could you make a local compiler experiment that changes the generated memory operations and report the resulting TFLOPs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made a local change in GenericSwizzling.cpp that forces this case through ld/st rather than ldmatrix/stmatrix. It measures 442 TFLOPs; my good baseline is 435 and the bad baseline is 359. I ran all of them twice on a 750W B200 without changing GPU clocks.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The alternate lowering remains around 359 TFLOPs and does not reduce the regression.
The alternate lowering reaches 438 TFLOPs rather than 442, still approximately matching the good baseline.

edges.comment: From c11. This local compiler modification is a diagnostic benchmark, not a persistent user-system change and not the final merged fix.

question_patterns: Can you isolate the behavior by toggling relevant compiler passes and rerunning the same benchmark?
Does disabling one of the layout optimization passes restore the previous performance?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Disabling optimize_tmem_layouts gives me 435 TFLOPs. With that pass disabled, the benchmark is back at the good baseline.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Disabling the layout optimization pass makes no difference; the result remains around 359 TFLOPs.

edges.comment: From c13-c15. Participant2 first read the IR and suggested that the tmem_load layout choice was producing the conversion; participant4 then measured the result of disabling the pass. Only the raw toggle result is placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you narrow the pass-level result to the individual rewrite or pattern responsible?
Which part of that compiler pass must be disabled to reproduce the restored performance?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No individual pattern reproduces the result; performance is restored only when the entire pass is disabled.
I isolated the same pattern, but only after testing the patterns in a different order.

edges.comment: From c16-c20. Participant4 isolated TMemLoadReducePattern and later volunteered that a fix was available in PR 8353. Participant2 noted that broadly disabling the pattern could add an extra memory round trip and that a better pass-level fix was preferable.

solution.intent: Apply the linked compiler fix for the tmem-layout problem that leaves a costly conversion in the flex_attention_fwd loop, then rerun the same B200 TritonBench cases on a build containing the fix before declaring the regression resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Land the fix proposed in PR 8353 for the diagnosed tmem layout and loop-conversion problem, then benchmark the same three noop flex_attention_fwd shapes on a build containing it. The reporter's post-merge run averaged 494.838 compiled TFLOPs.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter and collaborator supplied the unchanged TTGIR, PTX differences, NCU traffic increase, and benchmark results from compiler toggles. Interpreting those results as a poor tmem_load layout choice that introduces a costly convert_layout in the loop is the engineer-side diagnosis from c13-c18. The thread links the final PR but does not spell out its exact implementation, so the fix should not be described more specifically than the stated tmem-layout and loop-conversion issue.

edges.comment: From c20-c21. The reporter announced the fix PR, then closed the issue with a post-merge B200 benchmark averaging 494.838 TFLOPs. That benchmark is terminal-side verification and is deliberately excluded from required_info.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a poor tmem_load layout choice associated with TMemLoadReducePattern, leaving a costly convert_layout in the attention loop whose bad lowering uses more ldmatrix/stmatrix operations and greatly increases shared-memory traffic.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the unchanged TTGIR, changed PTX lowering, NCU shared-memory traffic, and the benchmark results from the alternate-lowering and pass-isolation tests.

Must apply or recommend the linked tmem-layout fix; forcing all such conversions through ld/st or disabling the whole optimization pass may be cited as diagnostic evidence, but must not be presented as the merged resolution.
No completed revert or failed fix was established in the thread, so the response must not invent a falsified revert branch or claim that a revert resolved the issue.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the B200 TritonBench cases on a build containing the fix and must not declare resolution until that verification restores performance.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical GPU performance engineer working with Triton compiler IR, generated PTX, NCU traces, local compiler patches, and stable B200 benchmarks; collaborators investigating the same deployment are folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, quantitative, and collaborative; supplies exact commits, benchmark tables, compiler artifacts, small experimental diffs, and direct follow-up measurements.
